materials: Carved obsidian, polished basalt, basalt dust pigment, smoked glass, charred cedar panel grain, blackened copper leaf, incense ash, volcanic sand, bone-white mineral wash, muted sea-glass enamel, dry graphite, oxidised bronze powder and thin translucent glazes.
palette: Obsidian black, basalt grey, incense ash, smoked charcoal, weathered cedar brown, blackened copper, tarnished bronze, salt-grey, deep sea-glass green, muted turquoise, dull kingfisher blue, ember orange, bullfinch rose, soft barn-owl ivory, bone cream and minute goldcrest yellow. Colours should appear as restrained mineral flashes rather than bright decoration.
composition: Landscape format with a wide, low-lit central chamber constructed from overlapping black reflective slabs. A large circular ash field sits slightly off-centre, crossed by vertical charred-wood grain lines that suggest tree trunks without becoming a literal forest. The birds are arranged as ritual presences around and within this structure: one immediate pale form held in the main ash circle, smaller incised and copper-lit forms distributed along the bark-like verticals and glass edges. The composition should feel balanced, spacious and architectural, with a broad quiet horizon implied by the reflective plane near the lower third.

creative_dna.palette_type: restrained nocturnal mineral palette with muted coastal greys, blackened metals, bone ivory and small sea-glass, ember, rose and yellow accents
creative_dna.complexity: refined moderate complexity with spacious negative space and carefully placed bird details
creative_dna.surface: glossy obsidian planes, smoked-glass reflections, ash-soft gradients, charred timber grain, shallow relief carving, incised copper lines and mineral washes
creative_dna.geometry: wide horizontal landscape structure with overlapping reflective slabs, off-centre circular ash field, vertical trunk-like grain lines and shard-like black glass forms
creative_dna.overall_character: A premium dark ritual chamber artwork where recognisable birds emerge from ash, carving, reflection and mineral colour; quiet, architectural, coastal-northern and mysterious without becoming gothic or literal.

materials: Urushi lacquer over kiri wood panels, rice-straw underlayer for subtle irregular relief, translucent celadon-green lacquer veils, muted vermilion lacquer ground, crushed eggshell inlay for the Barn Owl, powdered mica for Goldcrest glint and cool atmospheric shimmer, fine charcoal-black lacquer linework for reeds and bark marks, mineral pigments for restrained bird accents, silk-hinge references between panel divisions, and softly abraded surface textures suggesting salt-worn polish and weathered harbour wood.
palette: Vermilion ground muted under translucent celadon lacquer, deep black-brown urushi, smoke grey, sea-glass green, pale eggshell white, powdered mica silver, soft sandstone beige, weathered wood taupe, restrained bullfinch rose, kingfisher turquoise-blue and a single disciplined woodpecker red. Summer should appear as warmth beneath the lacquer rather than obvious seasonal colour.
composition: A horizontal six-panel screen structure with alternating dense and empty zones. The left third contains mostly open lacquer with a few reed marks and a concealed Treecreeper moving along a bark-like vertical seam. The central area holds the clearest bird presence, with the Kingfisher placed low-to-mid height as a sleek celadon stroke crossing a quiet reed interval. A pale Barn Owl form hovers in the upper right as fractured eggshell inlay, softened into the lacquer field. The Bullfinch, Long-tailed Tit, Goldcrest and Great Spotted Woodpecker occupy smaller rhythmic positions across the remaining panels, creating a slow visual walk rather than a crowded bird arrangement.

creative_dna.palette_type: Muted celadon-over-vermilion lacquer palette with black-brown urushi depth, eggshell white, smoke grey, sea-glass green, mica silver and restrained bird accents
creative_dna.complexity: Layered but restrained, with slow-revealing bird forms and delicate material detail
creative_dna.surface: Deep polished lacquer, translucent, inlaid, subtly relieved, salt-softened and quietly luminous
creative_dna.geometry: Horizontal six-panel folding-screen structure with asymmetrical spacing, vertical panel intervals, sparse reed strokes and off-centre bird placements
creative_dna.overall_character: A refined contemporary lacquer screen where negative space, celadon light, polished depth and precise inlaid birds create an intimate northern atmosphere of quiet observation

materials: Dichroic glass, UV-reactive acrylic, anodised aluminium armatures, micro-servo inspired rotational joints, fibre-optic points, translucent projection film, transparent resin lenses, optically coated mirrors, programmable daylight LEDs, frosted acrylic haze, lightly brushed metal, and subtle salt-worn surface textures translated into digital grain.
palette: Sea-glass turquoise, kingfisher cyan, soft barn-owl white, warm chalk, muted sandstone, pearl grey, smoked harbour blue, translucent rose, bullfinch coral, tiny gold-yellow, moss-olive shadow, ink black, ivory, and brief lacquer-red accents. Keep saturation selective: most of the image should be pale, airy and optically clear, with colour arriving as refined pulses.
composition: A landscape-format suspended atrium constellation with a broad, open horizontal drift. The central field is composed of overlapping glass planes and slender aluminium arcs that seem to rotate around an invisible axis. Leave quiet margins and a low, almost imperceptible horizon of diffused light. Position the most intense turquoise refraction slightly off-centre so the composition has energy without drama. Smaller bird-signals orbit and climb through the structure in measured intervals, creating a sense of slow kinetic movement across the screen.

creative_dna.palette_type: Pale coastal prismatic with selective saturated avian pulses
creative_dna.energy: Calm, weightless, radiant, slow-kinetic, quietly joyful
creative_dna.complexity: Refined medium-high complexity with spacious negative space and precise layered details
creative_dna.surface: Translucent, reflective, frosted, lens-like, sea-glass smooth with subtle salt-worn texture
creative_dna.geometry: Suspended horizontal constellation of rotating planes, slender arcs, lens ovals, offsets, halos and avian reduction marks
creative_dna.overall_character: An elegant northern-summer atrium installation where recognisable birds emerge as luminous optical events within a spacious architecture of moving glass, refraction and restrained colour

materials: Hand-spun flax, nettle fibre, hemp warp, raw wool, straw cord, dyed linen thread, madder, weld, woad and walnut husk dyes, stitched linen labels, tiny dulled tin sequins for starling sheen, horsehair edging, visible mending threads, irregular rya tufts and flattened kilim-like woven passages. The digital artwork should simulate these materials with convincing fibre grain, stitched relief, uneven dye absorption and soft shadowing appropriate for a premium wall-hung textile.
palette: Flax cream, oat straw, bleached hemp, pale sandstone, sea-glass green, woad blue, soft weld yellow, muted madder rust, walnut brown, civic pigeon grey, gull white, crow black, starling charcoal with tiny blue-green tin glints, and a restrained flash of Blue Tit yellow and blue.
composition: A landscape-format soft wall hanging divided into uneven horizontal crop-bands rather than a literal scene. The lower third is dense, tactile and trampled, built from short fibre, knots and darker seed-stitches. The middle register carries most of the bird emblems in a loose communal procession, partly embedded into the weave. The upper third opens into pale, thinned warp and cool air, with larger intervals of linen ground and softened horizontal drift. Edges should feel hand-bound and slightly weathered, with horsehair or dark thread edging creating a refined but imperfect frame.

creative_dna.dominant_family: architectural textile-register / contemporary woven wall hanging

creative_dna.complexity: layered and intricate but restrained, with embedded bird emblems, repaired seams, seed marks and varied visibility
creative_dna.surface: tactile, fibrous, weathered, hand-worked, mended, softly shadowed, unevenly dyed
creative_dna.geometry: uneven horizontal crop-bands, softened kilim geometry, broken chevrons, exposed warp threads, stitched markers and irregular woven intervals
creative_dna.overall_character: a premium landscape-format field-cloth: monumental yet modest, salt-softened and summery, carrying recognisable common birds as woven signs within a refined architectural textile structure

materials: Tin-glazed earthenware, cobalt oxide brushwork, copper-green glaze, manganese purple, antimony yellow, raised white slip, crackle glaze, hand-painted tile transfers, shell-impressed ceramic borders, milky grout, pearl lustre overglaze, lightly abraded glaze edges and subtle sandstone-toned underpainting.
palette: Tin white, Delft cobalt, copper sea-glass green, soft turquoise, manganese purple-black, antimony yellow, diluted sandstone beige, pearl lustre, pale grey grout, weathered wood brown and a few muted starling iridescences of petrol blue, violet and green.
composition: Landscape format. Arrange the image as a tiled bathhouse wall divided by a low horizontal waterline of wave-pattern courses. Above it, a large cobalt crest panel anchors the centre-left, surrounded by mismatched square tiles and oval bird medallions. Repeated pigeon motifs create a gentle architectural rhythm across the lower band. Smaller shell-bordered niches sit toward the corners and edges. A severe vertical manganese interruption offsets the decorative order on one side, preventing the design from becoming too sweet. Leave areas of pale tile and grout breathing space so the work remains calm and contemporary.

creative_dna.palette_type: cool maritime tin-glaze palette with Delft cobalt, sea-glass greens, milky whites, pale grout, muted lustre and restrained warm sandstone accents
creative_dna.energy: calm, buoyant, communal, quietly playful, salt-washed
creative_dna.complexity: moderately intricate ornamental tile system with legible bird emblems, layered glaze detail and breathing space
creative_dna.surface: luminous crackled ceramic wall with softened grout, glaze pooling, raised slip outlines, lustre flashes and hand-made irregularity
creative_dna.geometry: landscape tiled bathhouse wall with square and rectangular grids, oval medallions, wave courses, shell-bordered niches, a low horizontal waterline and one severe vertical interruption
creative_dna.overall_character: premium contemporary ceramic installation: a cool northern summer bathhouse of light, salt, glaze and geometry where common birds become refined resident emblems within a shared ornamental habitat

movement: Lime Orchard Fresco: The Five Small Citizens
materials: Wet lime plaster ground, marble dust intonaco, sinopia underdrawing, terre verte wash, yellow ochre, lime-safe ultramarine, iron oxide red, pale umber, bone black, casein secco retouching, rubbed pumice abrasion, shallow incised plaster lines, softened dry-brush dusting and minute embedded summer grit for a salt-worn mineral surface.
palette: Lime white, warm plaster cream, sandstone beige, yellow ochre, pale umber, terre verte, softened brick red, lime-safe ultramarine, blue-grey, muted lemon yellow, iron oxide red, dove grey, bone black, with faint sea-glass green and cool North Sea blue undertones worked into the shadows.
composition: A wide horizontal fresco wall divided into three shallow arcade bays and a pale upper lunette. The lower band carries small cracks, masonry ledges and seed-like marks where the two sparrows gather at slightly different distances. The middle band holds a curved lemon branch supporting the Blue Tit and opening the central rhythm. The Goldfinch crosses the central arch in a poised diagonal, giving the whole wall a gentle pulse. The Collared Dove rests high in the lunette as a pale balancing form. The structure should feel stable, airy and architectural, with generous unpainted plaster breathing between figures.

creative_dna.dominant_family: contemporary lime fresco civic orchard mural

creative_dna.energy: calm, sun-warmed, civic, intimate, lightly formal, airy and gently pulsed by the central goldfinch diagonal
creative_dna.complexity: moderate and carefully ordered: five clearly integrated bird citizens within a spare three-bay architectural orchard structure, reduced detail and generous negative space
creative_dna.surface: salt-softened lime intonaco, weathered mineral plaster, rubbed and abraded, with visible underdrawing, shallow cracks, incisions, dry fresco texture and breathable matte depth

creative_dna.overall_character: a discovered fragment of a humane northern garden-court wall-cycle: Renaissance calm refined into spare modern geometry, mineral colour and quiet civic bird presence without literal seaside imagery or decorative wildlife realism

movement: Prussian Weather Bureau for Seven Birds
materials: Cyanotype chemistry on oversized cotton-rag blueprint paper, UV contact exposure, translucent drafting film, graphite survey marks, white gouache erasures and corrections, pale archival masking tape, punched registration holes, dry embossing, archival pins, ruled meteorological annotations, lightly abraded paper edges and minimal transparent sea-glass tinted washes.
palette: Saturated Prussian blue, exposed chalk white, faded cyan, sea-glass green-blue, pale sandstone paper warmth, graphite grey, soft masking-tape beige and tiny restrained accents of goldfinch yellow and great tit green-black only where needed for recognition.
composition: A landscape-format meteorological chart fills the frame, with broad diagonal isobars sweeping from lower left to upper right. The lower margin holds clustered sparrow evidence like contact shadows near a measuring scale. A large, soft Wood Pigeon pressure-cell occupies the left-centre field. A small radiant Goldfinch compass burst sits slightly above centre as a crisp point of colour. A Chiffchaff song trace vibrates as a fine notation line across the midline. A Yellow-legged Gull is held high as a long white vector near the upper register. A Great Tit appears inside a circular sun gauge to the right, clean and emblematic. Leave generous blue space so the artwork feels calm, architectural and breathable.

creative_dna.palette_type: luminous Prussian-blue monochrome with exposed chalk whites, faded cyan, sea-glass blue-greens, pale paper warmth, graphite neutrals and tiny restrained bird-recognition accents
creative_dna.energy: lucid, breezy, serene, high-pressure, quietly elated
creative_dna.complexity: moderate-to-high but spacious, disciplined and breathable
creative_dna.surface: premium archival blueprint surface; cotton-rag, sun-exposed, salt-worn, taped, embossed, pinned, abraded and lightly corrected by hand

creative_dna.overall_character: a calm northern coastal summer weather document where seven recognisable birds are translated into cyanotype evidence, pressure forms, silhouettes, vectors and survey traces within a precise yet quietly luxurious Prussian-blue atlas

movement: Monsoon Miniature Aviary: A Burnished Folio of Summer Calls
materials: Handmade wasli paper texture, burnished agate sheen, opaque gouache, shell gold, lapis and malachite mineral colour, saffron staining, indigo wash, carbon-black hairline drawing, gum arabic gloss, microscopic white stippling, pierced-paper border effects and fine squirrel-hair brushwork translated into a contemporary digital artwork for a landscape Samsung Frame display.
palette: Lapis lazuli blue, sea-glass turquoise, malachite green, orpiment yellow, carmine lake, saffron glaze, shell gold, sandstone rose, pigeon mauve-grey, indigo shadow, warm parchment, salt-white stippling and muted harbour green-black.
composition: A landscape illuminated folio arranged as a wide charbagh garden viewed from above. Four narrow water channels cross at a small square pool near the centre, creating a calm geometric anchor. Flowering beds extend horizontally like an opened manuscript, framed by pierced borders and hairline gold rules. A narrow upper register holds a pale cloud band; a lower terrace band introduces architectural balance. The composition should feel spacious despite the ornament, with breathable intervals of burnished paper and cool blue wash.
